source.citation: Huffman, T.N. & Woodborne, S. (2021). New AMS dates for the Middle Iron Age in the Mapungubwe landscape. South African Journal of Science, 117(3/4), Article 8980. https://doi.org/10.17159/sajs.2021/8980

table_2.title: Population dynamics for the South African portion of the Shashe-Limpopo valley

method_as_described_by_authors.population_allocation_rule: The authors divide the time span of each facies by 50-year units, then estimate people per interval from site counts and include capital populations.
method_as_described_by_authors.special_k2_rule: The initial 25 years of K2 are represented as half of a 50-year unit. Later K2 and initial K2 subinterval estimates are both printed in the same table row.
method_as_described_by_authors.basis_cited_by_authors: Middle Iron Age burials at Kgaswe, Botswana

caveats: These are estimates produced by the authors' site-count/homestead-duration/population rule, not census observations.
The 50 people per homestead and 50-year homestead duration assumptions are model assumptions informed by an external burial comparison; they are not exact measured values for every site.
The table reports general population, capital population, and totals. Null capital population for Leokwe is the table's printed 'none' and is not a missing value.
The K2 row contains two subinterval estimates (125 years and 25 years); do not add or average them without preserving their different temporal meanings.
Use as a published derived-estimate target or prior with sensitivity analysis, not as hard ground truth.

table_3.title: Baobab climatic sequence and severe droughts recognised in the archaeological record

columns.cal_ad: Calendar AD interval/year in the article's archaeological column
columns.baobab_cal_ad: Baobab-calibrated calendar AD estimate(s) as printed by the source

interpretation_claims.statement: The authors identify drought Group IX at about AD 1310±5 as contributing to the abandonment of Mapungubwe, with political instability and loss of leadership legitimacy proposed as mediating processes.
The authors report that dates from Weipe508 indicate Mapungubwe occupation persisted in the valley until about AD 1320, approximately contemporaneous with the Group IX drought.
interpretation_claims.source_locator: PDF page 4, paragraph beginning 'Dates from Weipe508'

caveats: Table 3 is an event/sequence summary, not a continuous rainfall time series.
The baobab values are preserved as printed. A value with mean/sigma is not expanded into a probability distribution without the original proxy/calibration model.
The three VIII baobab values (1208, 1226, 1256) are kept as discrete reported values; no uncertainty was supplied in the table cells.
Blank archaeological or baobab entries are not interpreted as no drought or no occupation.
Group IX as a cause of abandonment is an author interpretation. It must be tested alongside political, trade, settlement and other environmental mechanisms.

limitations: Transcribed from published Tables 2 and 3; not independently reviewed.
Source PDF bytes are not locally available in this environment; source_pdf_sha256 remains null.
Table 2 estimates are not empirical census observations.
Table 3 does not provide raw baobab isotope series, proxy calibration model or complete drought-event uncertainty.
The exact transformation from the baobab δ13C proxy curve to event timing requires the cited underlying proxy publications.
next_steps: Second-person review of all Table 2 and Table 3 values against the publisher PDF page image.
Retrieve and hash the exact source PDF bytes before promoting source snapshot status.
Locate raw baobab isotope and calibration data and reconstruct uncertainty rather than interpolating the summary table.
Use Table 2 only as a published derived-estimate target with sensitivity over per-homestead population and occupation duration assumptions.
Preregister climate-only versus multi-causal experiments before comparing fit.
